## What you will learn

- The limits of plain Parquet
- The transaction log and ACID writes
- `MERGE`, time travel and schema enforcement
- `DELETE`, `UPDATE`, `RESTORE`, `OPTIMIZE` and `VACUUM`

---

## The limits of plain Parquet

| Problem | Example |
|---------|---------|
| **No atomicity** | A job fails during `overwrite`: the table is left half-written |
| **No UPDATE/MERGE** | A status update forces rewriting the partition or table |
| **Inconsistent reads** | A reader sees old and new files mixed during a write |
| **No history** | You cannot see what the table looked like yesterday |
| **Unprotected schema** | A file with different columns silently corrupts the table |

---

## The transaction log

```
  silver_delta/
  ├── _delta_log/
  │   ├── 00000000000000000000.json   <- v0: add files A, B, C
  │   ├── 00000000000000000001.json   <- v1: remove B, add D   (MERGE)
  │   └── 00000000000000000002.json   <- v2: remove A          (DELETE)
  ├── order_date=2024-07-01/part-....parquet
  └── order_date=2024-07-02/part-....parquet
```

Data stays in Parquet. The log says **which files make up each version**. Writing is atomic: either the log file of the new version exists, or the version never happened.

---

## MERGE (upsert)

```python
(orders_dt.alias("t")
 .merge(updates.alias("s"), "t.order_id = s.order_id")
 .whenMatchedUpdateAll(condition="s.updated_at > t.updated_at")
 .whenNotMatchedInsertAll()
 .execute())
```

The condition `s.updated_at > t.updated_at` protects against late data: an old event that arrives later does not overwrite a newer state.

---

## History and time travel

Each operation creates a new version. Old versions stay readable until `VACUUM` removes them.

```python
orders_dt.history().select("version", "timestamp", "operation").show()

v0 = spark.read.format("delta").option("versionAsOf", 0).load(SILVER_DELTA)

spark.sql(f"SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM delta.`{SILVER_DELTA}` "
          "VERSION AS OF 0 GROUP BY status")
```

---

## Schema enforcement & evolution

Delta **refuses** writes with an incompatible schema. Intentional changes are explicit:

```python
(with_coupon.write.format("delta")
 .mode("append")
 .option("mergeSchema", "true")     # old rows get null
 .save(SILVER_DELTA))
```

---

## DELETE, UPDATE & RESTORE

```python
orders_dt.restoreToVersion(merge_version)
orders_dt.delete(F.col("customer_id") == customer)
orders_dt.update(
    condition="status = 'created' AND created_at < '2024-07-03'",
    set={"status": F.lit("expired")},
)
```

::: {.callout-warning}
After a `DELETE`, the data still exists in the Parquet files of old versions and time travel can read it. For a real deletion (e.g. LGPD), you must run `VACUUM`.
:::

---

## OPTIMIZE & VACUUM

| Command | What it does | When |
|---------|-------------|--------|
| `OPTIMIZE` | Compacts small files into larger ones | After many MERGEs/appends |
| `OPTIMIZE ... ZORDER BY (col)` | Also reorganizes data to skip more blocks when filtering on `col` | Heavily filtered columns outside the partition |
| `VACUUM` | Deletes files that no recent version uses | Periodically; the default keeps 7 days |

---

## Summary

| Delta Lake | Command |
|------------|---------|
| Upsert | `DeltaTable.merge(...).whenMatchedUpdateAll().whenNotMatchedInsertAll()` |
| History | `.history()` / `DESCRIBE HISTORY` |
| Time travel | `.option("versionAsOf", n)` / `VERSION AS OF n` |
| Undo | `.restoreToVersion(n)` |
| Evolve schema | `.option("mergeSchema", "true")` |
| Compact | `.optimize().executeCompaction()` / `.executeZOrderBy(col)` |
| Clean old versions | `.vacuum(hours)` |
